commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds features to the application in the current directory: its files and its record become those of an application that was created with them. A feature the application already has is left as it is. A feature takes the place of one the application has by default, as postgres takes that of h2, and the command says which it replaces; a feature that was asked for by name, when the application was created or added to, is replaced only with --replace, and an option the application was created with is never replaced. The files you changed keep your changes. When a feature changes or takes out what you changed too, or a file it writes is there already, nothing is written and the files are named. An application with the feature of a feature pack that is not part of Grails gets a feature only with that very pack: the jar of a plugin is fetched again by the coordinates and the SHA-256 its record has, and the pack of a directory is given again with --feature-pack-dir.

options.description: Show the changes that would be made to the files, as a diff, and change nothing.
Say which files would be added, changed and removed, which features would be replaced, and which conflicts there are, and change nothing.

When the option is given, only the repositories it names are asked; without it, those of GRAILS_REPO_URL, Maven Central and then the repository the record of the application names for the jar. Can be given more than once.

options.label: URL
options.description: The plugin index to read in the place of that of Grails. The address is https, or file: for a file; none is for no plugin index, which leaves the plugins of this release of Grails. Without the option the GRAILS_PLUGIN_INDEX environment variable names the index, and without that the plugin index of Grails is read.
Lists the snapshot versions among the versions as well.
Show full stack trace when exceptions occur.
Create verbose output.
Print version information and exit.
